simple.meaning: מַהֲלָךְ (mahălâk) is a Hebrew word meaning “a walk , i.e. a passage or a distance.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַהֲלָךְ (H4109) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Nehemiah 2:6, with occurrences in Nehemiah, Ezekiel, Jonah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַהֲלָךְ (H4109) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַהֲלָךְ (H4109) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַהֲלָךְ (mahălâk) / H4109 is traced through Nehemiah 2:6, Ezekiel 42:4, Jonah 3:3, Jonah 3:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: The king said to me (the queen was also sitting by him), “How long will your journey be? When will you return?”
Before the rooms was a walk of ten cubits’ width inward, a way of one cubit; and their doors were toward the north.
So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to Yahweh’s word. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across.
Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”
